lead: Air is humidified when water evaporates into it and dehumidified when water leaves it. Both are moves on the psychrometric chart: heating, cooling, adding water, removing water, or mixing two air streams. A spray of recirculated water humidifies air along a wet-bulb line and stops at saturation. Cooling below the dew point, liquid desiccants, solid adsorbents and compression remove water. These operations set the air condition in rooms, drying plants and cooling towers. Here Y is the humidity ratio: kg of water vapour per kg of dry air.
prereq: You need: humidity terms, the psychrometric chart, adiabatic saturation and wet-bulb temperature, and Unit 3 for NTU and the enthalpy driving force.

blocks.text: Humidification means adding water vapour to air. Three common methods do this in different ways.

Spray chamber or air washer. Air passes up through a chamber while water sprays down from nozzles. A mist eliminator removes drops. The water collects in a basin and is pumped back. With no external heating or cooling, the recirculated water settles at the adiabatic saturation temperature, and the air follows a wet-bulb line. The air can only approach saturation; it cannot cross the saturation curve.

Wetted-surface humidifier. Air flows over a wet pad or wetted plates. Water evaporates from the surface. This is simple and is used in evaporative coolers and small air-conditioning units. The pad must stay wet and clean.

Steam injection. Dry steam is injected into the air duct. It adds water vapour and heat together. The humidity rises; the dry-bulb temperature also tends to rise. It is used in clean rooms and hospitals where fine control and no water droplets are needed.

In spray chambers and wetted-surface humidifiers the driving force is the difference between the vapour pressure at the water surface and the partial pressure of water vapour in the air. Steam injection adds moisture by direct mixing, not by evaporation from a surface.
Dehumidification means removing water vapour. A cold surface, a liquid desiccant, a solid adsorbent or compression can do it.

Cooling below the dew point. Cool the air sensibly at constant humidity until its dew point. Further cooling makes water condense on the coil. The air then follows the saturation curve downwards. This is the usual room air-conditioner coil. The condensate must be drained.

Liquid absorption. A concentrated lithium chloride or glycol solution has a low water vapour pressure. Water vapour from the air dissolves into it. The solution becomes dilute and must be regenerated by heating. Absorption releases heat, so the air may need cooling afterwards.
Solid adsorption. Silica gel or activated alumina holds water on its surface. The bed must be regenerated with hot air. This gives very dry air, down to low dew points.

Compression. Compression raises the partial pressure of the water vapour while the saturation vapour pressure depends only on temperature, so the air becomes supersaturated and water condenses. Cooling the compressed air in an aftercooler lowers the saturation pressure further and removes more water. This is used in small compressed-air dryers.
A cold water spray is not a dehumidifier for ordinary air. Unless the water is below the air dew point, the spray can only humidify the air towards saturation.

sections.h3: Chart paths and packed humidifier design

blocks.text: On the chart, every operation is a path. Heating is a horizontal line to the right: Y is constant, relative humidity falls. Cooling is horizontal to the left until the dew point, then it bends down along the saturation curve and water condenses. Humidifying moves upward. An adiabatic spray follows a wet-bulb line. Dehumidifying moves downward, by cooling, desiccant or compression. Mixing two streams gives a point on the straight line joining them, fixed by the mass balance.
Packed humidifier design uses the same NTU idea as a packed absorber. The driving force is an enthalpy difference, not a concentration difference.

NTU = ∫ dH / (H<sub>s</sub> − H), from H<sub>in</sub> to H<sub>out</sub>
Z = HTU × NTU
HTU = G / (K<sub>H</sub>a)
blocks.where: H is the moist-air enthalpy (kJ per kg dry air); H<sub>s</sub> is the saturated-air enthalpy at the water temperature (kJ per kg dry air); NTU is the number of transfer units (dimensionless); HTU is the height of a transfer unit (m); Z is the packed height (m); G is the dry-air mass velocity (kg dry air per m² s); K<sub>H</sub> is the enthalpy transfer coefficient and a is the packing area per unit volume, so K<sub>H</sub>a is the volumetric enthalpy transfer coefficient.

blocks.text: For a spray chamber with recirculated water, the water temperature is nearly constant, so H<sub>s</sub> is nearly constant. Then: NTU = ln[(H<sub>s</sub> − H<sub>in</sub>)/(H<sub>s</sub> − H<sub>out</sub>)]. The design steps are: fix inlet and outlet air states; find H<sub>in</sub>, H<sub>out</sub> and H<sub>s</sub>; compute NTU; choose packing and flow to get HTU; multiply to get Z. A larger NTU means the outlet air is closer to saturation.

examples.question: 1000 kg dry air/h enters an adiabatic spray chamber at 35 °C with Y = 0.010 kg water/kg dry air and leaves at 25 °C. (a) Find the outlet humidity using a wet-bulb slope of 0.00042 kg/kg per K. (b) Find the water evaporated. (c) If the outlet air is cooled to 15 °C, find the water condensed. The saturation humidity at 15 °C is 0.0106 kg/kg.
steps: On the wet-bulb line the slope is about c<sub>s</sub>/λ ≈ 0.00042 kg/kg per K, where c<sub>s</sub> is the humid heat and λ is the latent heat of water. ΔY = 0.00042 × 10 = 0.0042 kg/kg.
At 15 °C the saturation humidity is Y<sub>sat</sub> = 0.0106 kg/kg. The excess water is 0.0142 − 0.0106 = 0.0036 kg/kg.
examples.answer: The outlet humidity is 0.0142 kg/kg dry air, 4.2 kg/h of water evaporates, and 3.6 kg/h condenses when the outlet air is cooled to 15 °C.
examples.check:
Y_in = 0.010
slope = 0.00042
dT = 35 - 25
Y_out = Y_in + slope * dT
water = 1000 * (Y_out - Y_in)
Y_sat15 = 0.0106
condensed = 1000 * (Y_out - Y_sat15)
print(round(Y_out, 4))
print(round(water, 4))
print(round(condensed, 4))

traps: A cold water spray is not a dryer: if the water is above the air dew point, it humidifies. Dehumidify by cooling below the dew point or with a desiccant.
Wet-bulb temperature and dew point are not the same. Wet bulb is reached by evaporative cooling; dew point is reached by cooling at constant Y.
Adiabatic humidification stops at saturation. Adding more spray does not raise Y beyond the saturation value at that wet-bulb temperature.
Steam injection adds water and heat together, so it is not the same as an adiabatic spray.
When cooling below the dew point, use Y<sub>sat</sub> at the final temperature for condensate, not at the initial dew point.

quiz.q: Name two methods of humidifying air.
quiz.a: Spray chamber (air washer) and wetted-surface humidifier; steam injection is a third.

quiz.q: Why does a recirculated-water spray stop humidifying when the air reaches saturation?
quiz.a: Water is at the adiabatic saturation temperature. At saturation the air cannot take more vapour at that wet-bulb temperature, so net evaporation becomes zero.

quiz.q: Air at 30 °C with Y = 0.012 kg/kg is cooled to 10 °C. Saturation humidity at 10 °C is 0.0076 kg/kg. Find the water condensed per 1000 kg dry air.
quiz.a: Excess = 0.012 − 0.0076 = 0.0044 kg/kg. Condensed = 1000 × 0.0044 = 4.4 kg per 1000 kg dry air.

quiz.q: A solid desiccant lowers air humidity but the air leaves warmer. Explain why.
quiz.a: Adsorption releases heat of sorption. The latent heat of the condensed water becomes sensible heat in the air, so dry-bulb rises even as Y falls.

quiz.q: What is the difference between cooling to the dew point and cooling below the dew point?
quiz.a: At the dew point condensation is just starting. Below the dew point water condenses, Y falls along the saturation curve, and the air becomes drier.

quiz.q: In a packed humidifier H<sub>in</sub> = 50, H<sub>out</sub> = 65 and H<sub>s</sub> = 90 kJ/kg dry air, with H<sub>s</sub> constant. Find NTU.
Why is an enthalpy driving force used for a packed humidifier rather than a humidity difference alone?
quiz.a: Heat and mass transfer happen together. Enthalpy combines temperature and humidity, and the saturated enthalpy at the water temperature gives one driving force along the wet-bulb line.

beyond: Not for the exam. Liquid-desiccant dehumidification is used in hospitals and ice rinks where low humidity matters, and membrane dehumidifiers are an active research area. Cooling towers in power plants use the same wet-bulb limit that appears in this chapter. Search for 'liquid desiccant dehumidifier', 'psychrometric chart air washer', and 'enthalpy transfer unit humidifier' to go further.
